Commentary.Commentary: Right then. This Irish win sets up Group B nicely with still one match left each for all four teams. With all teams in with a shout, it will be interesting to see how the rest of the matches in this group pan out. We have more Group B action coming up as West Indies take on Zimbabwe. The first ball is at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT). You can switch tabs and follow the action. Cheers.

Andy Balbirnie, the Irish skipper says that it was a pretty special partnership. Feels relieved that they got over the line and hopes that they can now take this momentum to their final group game on Friday against West Indies.

Richie Berrington, the skipper of Scotland says that they were pretty happy with the first innings. Adds that they were good with the ball in the start and got some wickets as well but have to give credit to Ireland to the excellent knock from Curtis. Ends by saying that they will learn from their mistakes and come back stronger.

Curtis Campher wins the Man of the Match award for his match-winning knock of 72 runs of 32 balls. Curtis Campher gets a bit emotional as he says he was struggling a bit after receiving some bad news from his family recently. Mentions that he is really happy that he could help his side. Adds they have gone up the gears and it is starting to come together now.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

Earlier in the innings, Scotland did very well with the blade. It was Michael Jones who stood out with the blade for them and received great support from Richie Berrington and Matthew Cross to get over the 170-run mark. It wasn't a great effort with the ball by Ireland but it proved to be enough as their batters completed the job later on.

Scotland were clinical with the new ball in their defense of a tricky total. Having put Ireland in a miserable position at the end of 10 overs, Scotland let it slip and lost their way with the ball since then. Nothing went their way and eventually suffered defeat from the jaws of victory.

Ireland lost both their openers inside the first five overs in their pursuit of 177. Ireland kept losing wickets at regular intervals and as a result, were reduced to 65-4 at the halfway mark. George Dockrell and Curtis Campher then resurrected the Irish innings and gave their side a new lease of hope. The pair stitched an unbeaten 119-run match-winning partnership. Ireland are still alive in the Men’s T20 World Cup 2022 courtesy of this memorable win.

A tremendous fight back from Ireland. It looked like they were out of the game at one stage but Curtis Campher and George Dockrell showed great grit and determination to get their side over the line. This is the highest ever run chase for Ireland in the T20 World Cup. For once we all thought that 176 would be more than enough. But Ireland have proved it that cricket being called a game of uncertainties is not without any reason.
FOUR! Fuller again, outside off. Curtis Campher drives it past cover for another boundary. Ireland win by 6 wickets.
FOUR! Fuller and on off, Curtis Campher drives it through covers for a boundary. Scores level now!
FOUR! A low full toss on off, Curtis Campher slices it over backward point for a boundary!
Bowls it on leg, George Dockrell digs it to mid off for one. 9 needed off 9 now!
Fuller and on off, George Dockrell drives it to extra covers and takes two. Excellent running!
A low full toss outside off, George Dockrell looks to play at it but misses.
FOUR! Half volley on middle, Curtis Campher drills this one down the ground over mid-off and collects another boundary. Brilliant batting by Curtis Campher.
Full on off, Curtis Campher drives it wide of deep cover and collects two more.
Almost a yoker on the off stump, Curtis Campher scoops it over backward point and comes back for a couple of runs. The deep cover fielder does the cleaning work.
Fuller and around off, Dockrell drills it to long-off for a single.
Full toss on off, Curtis Campher slogs it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A low full toss on off, Curtis Campher flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a brace. Fifty up for Curtis Campher!
Change of bowler. Safyaan Sharif  (2-0-20-1) is back into the attack now.
Fuller and on off, Curtis Campher flicks it towards backward square leg. The fielder chases it well. They collect three runs.
FOUR! Fuller and on off, Curtis Campher reverse sweeps it through backward point for a boundary!
TWO WIDES! Bowls it outside leg, George Dockrell looks to flick it but misses. The keeper misses it as well. They collect one.
Tossed up on off, Curtis Campher looks to drive it but gets a thick outside edge. It goes towards short third man. They cross.
Bowls it outside off, Curtis Campher looks to play at it but misses.
Fuller and on middle, George Dockrell eases it to long on for one.
Tossed up outside off, George Dockrell looks to loft it but misses.
FOUR! Fine shot. On a length and on off, Curtis Campher slaps it through point for another boundary. It's quite expensive over for Scotland. 35 needed from 24 now!
Change. Ireland need 35 runs off 24 balls now. The pressure is on Scotland now. Mark Watt is back into the attack for his final over. Can he pull things back?
Wide! Shorter one down leg, Curtis Campher lets it go.
Slightly shorter and on off, George Dockrell pulls it towards square leg for one.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Touch fuller and on off, George Dockrell heaves it over mid on for a boundary!
FOUR! Slightly shorter and on off, George Dockrell drills it through long off for a boundary!
A yorker on leg, Curtis Campher flicks it to square leg for one.
On a length and on off, Curtis Campher eases it to mid-wicket for a brace. Good running!
Full now, attacking the pads. Curtis Campher stays back and clips it towards mid-wicket. They take a single.
Wheal follows the batter down leg with a full one. George Dockrell nurdles it to mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Up and over! Scotland need to find some answers before it gets too late. This partnership is building at a rapid pace. A length ball, outside off. George Dockrell flays it over covers and finds the boundary.
On the pads, flicked to mid-wicket for one.

SIX! Sweet connection! Curtis Campher is seeing a football here it seems. Fraction short, on off. Curtis Campher stands tall and dispatches it over the mid-wicket for a biggie. The Irish fans are loving the fight back.
LEG BYE! Fuller, on middle and leg. Dockrell misses his flick. He gets rapped on the pads. They collect a leg bye.
LEG BYE! This is pushed through, outside leg. Dockrell misses his flick. The ball rolls to the leg side off the pads. They collect a leg bye.
This is pulled to square leg for one.

Curtis Campher shuffles across and slogs this full delivery to wide long on. The batters push hard for two and get two. There is an appeal for run out at the non-striker's end. The umpire takes it upstairs but the verdict comes in favour of Ireland.

FOUR! Runs are coming in thick and fast now. It is tossed up, outside off. Curtis Campher premeditates the scoop and goes through with the shot. The man at short fine is beaten and runs away for four.
Leask goes short again, on off. Curtis Campher heaves it across the line to deep square leg for a couple now.
Short one, down leg. Dockrell swivels and pulls it behind square on the leg side for a single.
This one is darted on the pads, Dockrell stays back and nudges it to mid-wicket. They take one and 100 is up for Ireland.
On off, this is driven towards wide long off. They comes back for tw quite comfortably.
Nicely played! It is full and on off. Curtis Campher reverse-sweeps it to third man. The batters take three before the fielder cuts it out.
Shorter, on off. Campher pulls it to deep mid-wicket. The ball does not carry to the man in the deep. They tale a couple.
Campher goes leg side, the bowler follows with a length delivery. Campher works it to backward point.
SIX! Curtis Campher getting into the act now. It is tossed up, full and on off. Curtis Campher gets low and slogs it over the mid-wicket fence,

FOUR WIDES! Ireland will surely won't mind this. It is looped up, angled down leg. George Dockrell misses his flick. The keeper also fails to pick it up, the ball beats the short fine leg fielder as well. The batters sneak in three runs while the umpire signals a wide.
So, 11 runs off the over. Touch short, on middle. Dockrell goes back and punches it into the off side off his back foot. Only for a run.
SIX! Goes straight into the crowd. A short ball, on off. George Dockrell stands tall and smokes it over the mid-wicket fence. Ireland need many of these now.
Slightly short, on off. Dockrell hangs back and swats it down to long on. The batters take two.
Loops it up, around off. Dockrell comes down the track but is unable to get it away.
A googly this time, quite short. Campher cuts it to the off side and crosses.
Fuller, attacking the stumps. Dockrell pushes it gently towards covers for a single.
Back of a length, on off. George Dockrell pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
This length ball is driven into cover, but straight at the fielder.

FOUR! A much-needed boundary for Ireland. It is full, hunting the blockhole. George Dockrell stays leg side of the ball and guides it through point by opening the face a touch late. The fielder in the deep makes a mess and the ball crosses the ropes.
Back of a length, outside off. George Dockrell looks to chase it but misses.
A length ball, on off, blocked out.
Short on the middle stump, George Dockrell pushes it to long-on.
On a length, outside off, punched to covers for one.
Flatter at the pads, Curtis Campher works this between deep mid-wicket and long-on and accumulates a couple of runs.
Short on the middle stump, George Dockrell pushes it to long-on and gets off the mark.

Drinks break! Ireland looks in all kinds of trouble here. They are four down already and they need to chase a huge total. Scotland have been amazing with the ball. None of their bowlers have leaked runs. They will look to continue with the same momentum. George Dockrell walks in next.

OUT! GONE! Good-length delivery on the off stump, Tector gets down his knees looking to slog sweep and clear cow corner. He doesn't get enough on the bat to clear the ropes and ends up spooning it to Chris Greaves at deep mid-wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Chris Greaves b Michael Leask

Commentary.Commentary: Short on the off stump, Campher plays it off the backfoot on the offside.
Short and on the leg stump, Harry Tector rocks back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
On off, this is played towards covers for one.
Fuller one on middle, Calum MacLeod flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Curtis Campher is the new man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Goes fuller and on middle, Lorcan Tucker looks to sweep it but gets a top edge. The ball carries towards short fine leg. Josh Davey settles under it and takes an easy catch. Pressure piling up on Ireland as they go three down now!
Commentary.Howout: c Josh Davey b Mark Watt

Commentary.Commentary: Slightly shorter and slower too, Lorcan Tucker looks to slap it but gets a bottom edge as the ball bounces off the deck.
Fuller and on leg, Lorcan Tucker just gives it a fine tickle towards fine leg for two.
Tossed up, on off. Lorcan Tucker nudges it to mid-wicket for a brace.
Flighted at the pads, Lorcan Tucker works it to deep mid-wicket for a single. Tidy first over by Chris Greaves.
Tossed up outside off, Lorcan Tucker gets forward and drives it to deep cover for a single.
Fuller and around off, Tucker sweeps it hard behind square for one.
WIDE! Flatter but down the legside, Lorcan Tucker lets it go.
Flighted on the middle stump, Harry Tector drives it to long-off.
Flighted outside off, Lorcan Tucker shuffles across and sweeps it behind square for a run.
Googly sliding onto the pads, Harry Tector clips it wide of long-on for a single.
Safyaan Sharif bowls it on off, this is pulled towards deep mid-wicket for one.
Slightly shorter this time, this is played towards deep covers for one.
Good length, on off. Lorcan Tucker taps it to backward point for a brace.
Fuller and on off, Harry Tector miscues his flick towards point for one.
FOUR! Length again, outside off. Harry Tector dances down the track and lofts it over mid off for a boundary!
On a length and outside off, Harry Tector looks to play at it but gets a bottom edge towards the keeper.
Good length outside off, Lorcan Tucker advances down the track to go inside out over covers but gets beaten once again.
Good-length delivery on the middle stump, Harry Tector clips it behind square to deep square leg for a single.
Good length outside off, Lorcan Tucker works it off the backfoot to short third man and takes a quick single.
Short and wide outside off, Harry Tector cuts it to the man at deep backward point.
Good length around off, Tector steers it to the cover region.
Slower and back of a length outside off, Harry Tector advances down the track and gets beaten.
FOUR! This should release some pressure. It is full, on middle, Lorcan Tucker shuffles and paddles it over short fine. It races away to the fence. A wicket-taking over by Sharif comes to an end.
Tector gets off the mark now! Fuller, on middle and leg. Tector get off side of the ball and nudges it to square leg for one.
On a length, outside off. Tector gets behind the line and blocks it away.
Harry Tector is the new batter.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! This review has put Ireland in a spot of bother. It all started with a huge appeal for caught behind but the umpire turned it down! It is a short ball, wide of off. Paul Stirling hangs back and slashes at it. The keeper thinks he has got a nick on it and is quite confident. Hence, Richie Berrington takes the review. The original decision is not out. The UltraEdge later confirms that there is a spike as the ball passes the blade. The umpire is asked to overturn his decision here. Great use of the review by Scotland yet again.
Commentary.Howout: c Matthew Cross b Safyaan Sharif

Commentary.Commentary: A length ball, angled into the body. Tucker tucks it to mid-wicket for a single this time.
WIDE! A slower ball, fraction short, wide of off. Tucker throws his blade at it but misses.

FOUR! Lorcan Tucker gets off the mark in fine fashion. He has come out with the right intent here. The footwork does the trick for him. It is a length ball, outside off. Lorcan Tucker steps down the track and drives it through covers for a cracking boundary. A pleasing shot to the eyes, this.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Paul Stirling defends it on the offside.
LEG BYE! A length ball, on middle and leg. Tucker misses his flick. The ball goes to the off side off the pads. They cross for a leg bye.
Short outside off, Lorcan Tucker advances down the track looking to slap it but gets beaten.
Peach of a delivery! Good length outside off, lures Lorcan Tucker into the flick and gets beaten.
Lorcan Tucker walks in.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Short of a length delivery, Andy Balbirnie punches it uppishly and straight to the fielder at point. Michael Jones dives forward and completes the catch. Balbirnie is distraught. Wheal's accurate bowling has rewarded him with success.
Commentary.Howout: c Michael Jones b Brad Wheal

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length delivery at the body, Andy Balbirnie clips it wide of deep square leg and comes back for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Paul Stirling ends the over on a positive note. It is touch short, on off. Paul Stirling shuffles, picks up the length early and pulls it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
A length ball, around middle, this one angles into leg. Paul Stirling tries to flick it away but misses.
Fraction short, outside off. Andy Balbirnie chops it towards point. One taken.

FOUR! Andy Balbirnie is switching gears here. It is a good-length ball, outside off. Andy Balbirnie stands tall and hammers it through cover-point for a boundary. Two fielders give it a chase but in vain.

DROPPED! A huge chance goes abegging! It is a length ball, on off. Paul Stirling looks to hoick it away but does not connect well. It lobs in front of mid on off the outer half. Calum MacLeod there sprints in front of him and puts in a forward dive. Although, the ball spills out in the end. Calum MacLeod prefers to stay on the ground and covers his face with the hat. How costly will the drop catch prove to be?
It is a length ball, on leg. Andy Balbirnie makes room and punches it to covers. The fielder there dives to his left to make a half-stop. The batters cross.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Andy Balbirnie moves to the offside and paddles it behind square to short-fine leg for a single.
Short of a length delivery, Andy Balbirnie defends it on the offside.
Good length angling into Stirling, gets into the line of the ball and plays it on the onside for a single.
Full outside off, Andy Balbirnie works it to deep backward point without moving his feet.
Short of a good length outside off, Paul Stirling pushes it to deep backward point.
Good length outside off, Paul Stirling goes for the drive to an outswinging delivery and gets beaten.
Ireland will have to put up a solid opening stand if they need to chase this total. Can they do it?
Tosses it up, outside off. Andy Balbirnie taps it towards point. A good over from Watt apart from the boundary.
Floated and full, on off. Andy Balbirnie taps it to covers.
On off, defended out watchfully.
FOUR! Finds the gap. It is pushed through quicker, full and outside off. Andy Balbirnie opens the face and drives it through cover. It is in the air for a while but goes through the gap.
Paul Stirling and Ireland are off the mark. It is full, on middle and leg. Paul Stirling leans forward and flicks it to mid-wicket for a single.
Watt comes around the wicket and goes full, on middle. Paul Stirling eases it back to the bowler.
